messages:
Kevin: Heads-up — I'm opening a PR to change the Python SDK's implicit routing behavior. Currently we infer routing from model name which often causes silent fallbacks + messy telemetry. Plan: make routing_policy an explicit optional arg and emit a DeprecationWarning when callers rely on implicit inference. Remove implicit inference in 2.0. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1337 :thinking_face:

Maria: Is the idea to break users immediately or do a soft deprecation window?

Kevin: Soft deprecation. 1.1 will add the warning + auto-fill via previous heuristic if not provided. 1.2 will start failing in strict mode (env var), 2.0 removes implicit fill. Goal is to avoid surprises in routing telemetry and make per-route cost visible.

Alex: Strong +1 for warnings. Also propose we add a runtime flag REDWOOD_STRICT_ROUTING that teams can flip to test their code paths before 2.0. That avoids surprises for customers with lots of microservices.

Sam: Telemetry question — will the SDK emit a distinct attribute/tag for routing_policy so Console dashboards can show usage by policy? Right now routes get lost under model name fallbacks.

Kevin: Yes, I'll add `sdk.routing_policy` to outgoing traces and to request metadata. That will be added in the same PR.

Jonathan: Can Product/Console UI add a migration view that surfaces services relying on implicit routing? We could show top callers that didn't set routing_policy in the last 30d and give them a one-click suggest change.

Sam: That would be super helpful. Without it, customers won't know what to change. Also need to ensure quotas/limits are applied using the final resolved policy so billing and guards match what the user expects.

Kevin: Agreed. We should also ensure quota evaluation uses the resolved policy on the server side — I'll file an infra ticket if that's not already the case.

devex-bot: CI / tests passed for branch `kevin/require-routing` — 14 changed files, 42 tests.

infra-ci: deploy-preview created at https://deploy-preview.redwood-inference.internal/1337 for review (test cluster).

Alex: One more edge: embeddings and reranking calls that are legacy wrappers — ensure the same warning surface. We should add a unified lint rule in the pyro/ts linters that flags `generate(... )` calls without routing_policy.

Maria: I'm happy to write the migration guide + example patterns. Proposed snippet for migration section:

```python
# old (implicit)
resp = client.generate("Summarize: " + doc)

# new (explicit)
resp = client.generate("Summarize: " + doc, routing_policy="low_latency")
```

Maria: I'll open a docs PR and include common mappings from model names -> routing_policy to help teams.

Sam: For multi-language support: TS/Go SDKs should mirror this change. Do we coordinate a simultaneous minor bump or staggered?

Kevin: Plan is: Python change first (because it's most used internally), then TS/Go follow within 2 weeks. We'll use the same deprecation pattern to keep behavior consistent.

Jonathan: Product will scope a Console card that shows dropped telemetry and a migration panel — will sync with you all on requirements tomorrow.

Kevin: Thanks. Maria — if you can own the migration docs + sample lints, we'll land the PR behind the `REDWOOD_STRICT_ROUTING` opt-in and roll warnings for a cycle. :thumbsup:

Maria: Taking it. I'll target a docs PR + lint rules by EOD Friday and ping here.

Kevin: Awesome — thanks everyone. Keeping the change small/timeboxed so we don't cascade other breaking changes.
